status-success.scope: Confirmations and positive states app-wide. As of 2026-09-04 also marks Daily Reports' PPE Compliant status control.

status-warning.scope: Caution states app-wide (e.g. unpriced records, pending attention). As of 2026-09-03 also used for Supplier Loads' Reactivated badge. As of 2026-09-04 also used for Daily Reports' PPE Missing-PPE status control and its Work Information required-but-empty badge.

status-danger.scope: Cancellation, destructive, and error states app-wide. As of 2026-09-04 also used for Daily Reports' initial-load error panel and its Problems/Delays/Incidents note panel.

calc-result.scope: Reserved exclusively for calculated/derived values. As of 2026-09-05 also correctly applied to Customers' Billed/Paid/Remaining balance tiles and Item Catalog's per-item unit-symbol chip — both genuinely calculated/reference values, replacing plain Ink tiles/text.

hero-text-warm.scope: Home screen only: text and symbols (title, eyebrow, hint) inside the Make Receipt hero card. Computed contrast against signal-orange is ~4.56:1 (WCAG AA normal-text pass). Not a general on-orange text color — every other orange surface in the app keeps white/cream text per the button and collapsible-header components below.

narrative.overview:
DROMEX is documented, not redesigned, here: every rule describes the interface as it actually ships in src/ui/theme.ts, src/ui/components/AppPrimitives.tsx, and the screen implementations, cross-checked against docs/design-system.md, which remains the authoritative source of record. Where the confirmed target direction differs from what ships today, that gap is named explicitly rather than folded into the current-system description.

DROMEX presents as a durable, organized field ledger for running a construction/plant operation: Structural Navy gives it authority and hierarchy, Ledger Cream stands in for paper record stock, and Signal Orange marks the one thing that matters most on a given screen — the action to take or the record that needs attention. The voice is sturdy, direct, and field-professional rather than decorative.

Domain separation (projects, loads, suppliers, fuel, equipment, safety, reports) is carried by grouping, labels, numbering, and icons — not by a unique color per domain. Color is otherwise reserved for role, not decoration.

Implemented on Home (2026-09-03): the two Approved Refinement Targets below (graded typography weight, restrained domain markers) ship on the Home screen via an opt-in `refined` prop on ExpandableMenuSection/MenuAction (see 'Menu Action Row (Refined)' and 'Section Marker Chip (Refined)'), plus a locally-scoped warm on-orange text color (`hero-text-warm`) for the Make Receipt hero card.

Implemented on Project Command Center (2026-09-03, two passes): the same two targets, plus a richer second layer gated behind a new, independent `polished` prop (always paired with `refined`, never alone) — an attached numbered ledger tab instead of an inline chip, a connected header/body folder seam (animated Signal Orange, static once settled), individually-shadowed white rows layered on the Ledger Cream body (see 'Menu Action Row (Polished)' and 'Section Ledger Tab (Polished)'), a capped staggered row reveal, and content-specific compositions including a real vertical timeline for the combined activity view. This second pass followed direct physical-review feedback that the first pass's mixed-color headers looked busy and its opened sections looked like generic cards.

Implemented on Supplier Loads (2026-09-03): an ambitious refinement of an already-approved, already-liked screen, not a replacement — its bespoke Structural-Navy-supplier/cream-tan-project/blue-gray-container hierarchy and Supplier-to-Project disclosure stayed exactly as shipped, and it was deliberately not migrated to ExpandableMenuSection. It is the first screen to implement the full 4-step typography target (900/700/600/500, see 'Supplied Material Record' above) rather than Home's and Project Command Center's 3-step subset, and introduces a Status-Warning Reactivated badge plus a locally-computed 'Trip N of M' connected-rail device for repeated same-day deliveries (see 'The Connected Trip Rule'). Domain visual identity was deliberately left untouched here, since its existing two-tier color hierarchy already serves that role.

Implemented on Daily Reports (2026-09-04): the per-project Daily Report editor's ten fixed sections adopt a third, independently-built bespoke Ledger Section device (see 'Daily Report Ledger Section' above) — a Structural Navy header, an attached Ledger-Cream numbered tab (01-10), a rotating +/x glyph, and a Signal-Orange-topped Ledger Cream body, closed by default. It is the second surface (after Supplier Loads) to use the full 4-step typography target, and the third (after Home and Project Command Center) to implement restrained numbered-marker domain identity, in both cases via fresh screen-local code rather than the shared ExpandableMenuSection/refined/polished mechanism. The whole-business Report Generation Excel-workbook section living in the same file was deliberately left untouched, including every style it depends on. The Daily Report PDF template's four summary cards, previously decorated in unrelated green/blue/orange/purple fills, were brought into compliance with the already-standing One Ledger Rule — a pre-existing violation corrected, not a new rule introduced — with semantic color now reserved for the PPE status column and the Problems/Delays/Incidents panel only.

Implemented on Business Directory Screens (2026-09-04/05): Financials, Workspace Hub's Business Directory grouping, Projects, Customers, People & Equipment, and Item Catalog were each audited and given full accessibility coverage, 48dp touch targets, consistent loading/empty/no-results states, and — on the five beyond Workspace Hub — a new, distinct pattern family: a Directory Hero Header (a Structural Navy banner with a live count summary, replacing a plain white header), a pill-shaped Search Bar, a dot-marked Status Pill (solid-tinted for active, outlined for inactive, so the states read apart without relying on hue alone), a Collapsible Status Band for closed-by-default secondary record groups, a Monogram Avatar for people/customer rows, and a Quiet Inline Action for lower-emphasis buttons. This is a separate improvement from the two Approved Refinement Targets above, not an extension of them — these six screens did not adopt the graded typography-weight scale (they kept their pre-existing weight-900/800-heavy usage) and the new hero/search/band/avatar pattern is about record-directory findability, not operational-domain wayfinding. Workspace Hub's own Business Directory section change was mechanical only: its existing `refined`/`marker` props, already proven on Home, applied to one more section.

Every other screen, and the global theme.ts type-scale tokens, remain on the base/default pervasive-weight-900, no-marker treatment described throughout this file.
keyCharacteristics: One consistent orange/navy/cream hierarchy reused across every screen, PDF, and spreadsheet export.
Color communicates role, not decoration — status colors mean status, the result teal means "this number was calculated," nothing else borrows those hues.

Bold, high-weight type used pervasively as the base/default treatment — except Home's and Project Command Center's navigation sections, which use a graded 900/700/600/500 hierarchy (see 'Implemented on Home' and 'Implemented on Project Command Center' above).
Rounded, card-based composition throughout; no bare unstyled lists or borderless flat sections.
Restrained, functional shadows: elevation appears only on floating/interactive elements, never as decoration on static content.

rules.name: The One Ledger Rule
rules.body: Every screen, PDF, and Excel export shares the same orange/navy/cream hierarchy. A new surface introducing its own palette is a defect, not a variant.

rules.name: The Reserved-Hue Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, red, and calc-result teal each mean exactly one thing (success, warning, danger, calculated value). None of the four may be reused for brand emphasis or decoration, and no other hue may be used for those four meanings.

rules.name: The Direct-Verb Rule
rules.body: Button and action labels are direct verbs describing the exact effect (Save Fuel Delivery, Open Report, Cancel Movement), never vague labels like "Submit" or "Go."

rules.name: The Tinted-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are colored from the element they fall from (brand-orange-deep under orange/warm elements, ink under neutral surfaces), never a generic flat black.

rules.name: The Seam Rule
rules.body: Wherever a collapsed/solid-color header opens into a lighter body, a colored rule marks the seam — 3px navy under an orange header, or an animated 3px orange bar that grows across an opening menu header. The seam is always present; it is never a plain, unmarked edge.

rules.name: The Hero-Only Warm Rule
rules.body: hero-text-warm (#FFFCF6) is used exclusively for text and symbols inside Home's Make Receipt card. No other orange surface in the app uses it; every other orange surface keeps white/cream text per the Buttons and Collapsible Filters components.

rules.name: The Numbered Marker Rule
rules.body: Every Home, Project Command Center, and Daily Reports navigation section carries a numbered index instead of a color-coded identity — Home as an inline Ledger-Cream chip, Project Command Center as an attached tab protruding above the header, Daily Reports as an independently-built attached tab of the same kind — restrained wayfinding via numbering and fill, not a dedicated hue per section, per the Reserved-Hue and One Ledger Rules. Home and Project Command Center implement it via the shared `marker` prop plus `refined` (Home) or `refined`+`polished` (Project Command Center); Daily Reports implements the same idea as screen-local code, not through that shared prop; the five base/default ExpandableMenuSection consumers, and Supplier Loads by explicit decision, do not use it.

rules.name: The Rotating Disclosure Rule
rules.body: Home's and Project Command Center's navigation sections animate one + glyph rotating 45 degrees into an × on open, instead of swapping between two separate glyphs. The base/default treatment used by the five other ExpandableMenuSection consumers still swaps + and × as instant text.

rules.name: The Connected Folder Rule (Project Command Center only)
rules.body: When a Project Command Center section opens, the header's bottom corners and the body's top corners both flatten, and a static 4px Signal Orange rule marks exactly where they meet, continuing the animated accent bar that grew across the header during the opening transition. Header and body must read as one opened folder, never as two stacked, unrelated cards. Home's refined sections do not use this connected treatment.

rules.name: The Refined/Polished Separation Rule
rules.body: `refined` and `polished` are independent props on ExpandableMenuSection/MenuAction. `refined` alone reproduces Home's exact shipped treatment; `polished` is Project Command Center's additional layer and must only ever be passed alongside `refined`, never alone. A future screen wanting Project Command Center's richer look opts into both explicitly; Home must never inherit `polished` behavior by accident.

rules.name: The Connected Trip Rule (Supplier Loads only)
rules.body: Supplier Loads visually connects repeated deliveries that share the same supplier, project, item, unit, transport signature, and calendar day with a restrained Structural Navy rail and a 'Trip N of M' badge — a display-only grouping computed locally in the screen, never merging the underlying records, totals, audit histories, correction state, or cancellation state. Each connected trip keeps its own independent edit/correct/cancel action. Different trucks or drivers are never grouped together.

rules.name: The Outlined-Inactive Rule
rules.body: A Status Pill's inactive/completed state is a transparent, outlined pill (line-colored border, muted dot and text), never a differently-tinted fill of the active state. Active/inactive must read apart by shape and fill, not only by hue, so the distinction survives grayscale, colorblindness, and bright field sunlight.

dos: Do reuse AppPage, PageHeader, AppCard, AppButton, AppField, MetricCard, Feedback, and EmptyState from src/ui/components/AppPrimitives.tsx for any new screen.
Do keep the calc-result teal exclusive to calculated/derived values; keep semantic (green/amber/red) colors exclusive to status.
Do mark the seam between a solid collapsed header and its lighter expanded body with a colored rule (the Seam Rule).
Do keep destructive (danger) actions visually separated from the primary action on every screen.
Do close large record sections by default and require an explicit tap to open them.

Do check all three render paths in ExpandableMenu.tsx before changing it — `refined` only (Home), `refined`+`polished` (Project Command Center), and neither (the five other screens) — they are meant to diverge, not to be merged for simplicity.
Do cap staggered row-reveal delays (e.g. min(index * 26ms, 220ms)) so a section with hundreds of records still finishes revealing in well under a second.
donts: Don't introduce a new brand hue outside Signal Orange / Structural Navy / Ledger Cream without a stated, non-decorative role.
Don't give a domain (fuel, safety, waste, etc.) its own strong brand color today — that isn't how the current system separates domains.
Don't place unrelated controls inside one card, or a paragraph inside a button.
Don't use a flat, uncolored black shadow — shadows are tinted from the element they fall from.

Don't treat the pervasive weight-900 usage across every text role as an intentional hierarchy device outside Home's and Project Command Center's refined/polished navigation sections — everywhere else it is still the current shipped base state, not a confirmed target.
Don't use hero-text-warm anywhere outside Home's Make Receipt card.
Don't pass the `polished` prop without also passing `refined` — it is an additive layer, not a standalone variant.
